newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Cabot Oil to grow by drillbit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Cabot Oil to grow by drillbit.

text.p: Cabot Oil & Gas Corp aims to grow its production mainly by an aggressive drilling program on its existing land holdings, including recently acquired properties in the U.S. Rocky Mountains.
Chief executive Charles Seiss told Reuters in an interview that the company planned to drill 256 wells this year after drilling 102 in the first half with a success rate of 90 percent.
"It started two and a half years ago when we decided to take a lot of cost out of the company and that acquisitions were becoming very expensive and entailed a lot of risk," Seiss said.
Houston-based Cabot's operations are in the Rockies, Appalachia, the Anadarko Basin in Oklahoma and the U.S. Gulf Coast.
The company last month reported record second-quarter net income of $2.0 million, or $0.09 per share.
Cabot is currently producing 187 million cubic feet per day of natural gas and expects that the year end figure would be above that.
It recently acquired proven reserves of 74 billion cubic feet of natural gas in 65 wells in the Rocky Mountains.

Seiss said that the company would like to cut its reserve life, currently 14.5 years, because Wall Street does not attach higher valuations for anything above 10 years, but would not look to go too low because that was too risky.
"I do not want a four to five year reserve life, where if the price were to go bad for two years those companies would consume large parts of of their reserves," he said.
Cabot also benefits from its own underground storage, which enables it to wait for a better price and a 3,400 mile pipeline system which means that it can command premiums over wellhead prices.
Seiss said Cabot "would like to be in the shallow offshore in the Gulf of Mexico. I would not see it necessarily this year. We could do it through a successful merger in that area," Seiss said.
